title: dedicated: autoscaler burst controls + per-fleet utilization reporting (v17)
author: Lena Thompson
description:
Motivation: dedicated fleets occasionally experience noisy scale-ups during short traffic spikes which increases cost and causes uneven tail latency. This PR implements a configurable burst window and soft-throttle policy in the Dedicated Fleet Autoscaler and adds per-fleet + per-zone utilization reporting to help operators tune autoscaling policies.

What this PR does: - Adds burst_window_ms and burst_max_instances fields to FleetAutoscaler policy config (defaults to 30s window, 20% burst capacity). - Implements a soft-throttle decision path that allows temporary burst capacity without immediate node provisioning; throttle is coordinated via tokens per-fleet to avoid cross-fleet contention. - Emits new metrics: redwood_dedicated_fleet_burst_events_total, redwood_dedicated_fleet_burst_duration_seconds, redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization_percent (labels: fleet_id, zone, model_family). - Adds a per-fleet utilization report endpoint to the control plane API (/v1/fleets/{id}/utilization?window=1h) and corresponding Console dashboard tiles. - Improves autoscaler leader-election to reduce duplicate scale actions under transient partitioning. - Adds migration logic: existing FleetAutoscaler objects get a safe default; explicit opt-in recommended for aggressive workloads.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for decision logic [x] integration test with mock scheduler [x] metrics emitted and scraped by e2e observability stack [x] Console tiles added [x] docs + release note drafted

Migration notes: This change is backward-compatible by default; customers who want identical pre-v17 scaling behavior can set burst_window_ms=0. Operators should monitor the new utilization metrics for 24-72h after enabling burst to tune burst_max_instances per fleet.

Performance: additional CPU for autoscaler leader is ~1-2% in 1k-fleet clusters; memory impact negligible. E2E tests show 15-35% reduction in unnecessary node provisions during 30-60s spikes in our staging workload.

Related: ENG-4821, ENG-5012, previous PR series v10-v16 (see linked PRs).
commits: Add burst window and burst_max_instances to FleetAutoscaler schema (autoscaler/api)
Implement soft-throttle token allocator and decision path (autoscaler/core)
Emit per-fleet utilization and burst metrics (observability/metrics)
Add control plane API endpoint and Console dashboard tiles (control-plane, redwood-console)
Leader election robustness fixes and additional e2e tests (autoscaler/e2e)
Docs: updated autoscaler config reference and migration guide (docs/operations)
review_conversation: Omar Khan: Nice work. Two questions: (1) how do we avoid token starvation when multiple fleets spike in the same zone? (2) can we add a flag to disable leader-optimizations for shards that are managed externally?

Lena Thompson: Token allocator uses a per-zone budget computed from current cluster headroom; if exhausted we fall back to nominal scale-up path. Added comment and unit tests covering simultaneous bursts across 3 fleets.
Miguel Santos: Found a race in leader election where duplicate scale writes could happen during transient network partitions. Please add compare-and-set on desired_capacity writes.
Lena Thompson: Addressed with CAS and added e2e that simulates partitioning (test case added). CI flaky test also fixed.
Aisha Patel: Metrics look good; suggest adding model_family label to utilization metric for easier breakdowns. Also please confirm cardinality impact.
Lena Thompson: Added model_family label; we aggregated to top-3 families in Console UI to limit cardinality. Documented in metrics section.
Grace Li: Approving after CI green and docs updated.
notes_for_release: Added burst control and per-fleet utilization reporting. New autoscaler policy fields (burst_window_ms, burst_max_instances). New metrics and Console tiles. Backward-compatible by default. Operators should review per-fleet utilization after enabling.
release_notes:
- Feature: burst_window_ms and burst_max_instances for Dedicated Fleet Autoscaler (defaults preserve previous behavior).
- Feature: per-fleet utilization reporting and Console dashboard tiles.
- Improvement: reduced unnecessary node provisions during short spikes.
- Ops: monitor redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization_percent after enabling.
testing_summary: Unit tests for allocator and policy; integration test against mock scheduler; e2e runs in staging with metrics verification. Observability smoke tests validate metric emission and Console tile render.
rollback_plan: Revert the autoscaler deployment and set burst_window_ms=0. If revert not possible, set fleet policy burst_max_instances=0 for affected fleets and rely on standard autoscaler behavior.
